title: Playing school and convent dances; Al Black sings I Believe
summary: He explains how he behaved as a gentleman at Gulf Coast schools and convents, and singer Al Black's number.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: They liked me because I treated professors with respect and I acted like a professor. I didn't act like a jazz musician, you know what I mean? And I always got the job. That at Gulf Paul College. That's a good school. And we drive up there and I want to get there at least 45 minutes, half hour at a time. Couldn't get in. I have to wait until the professor come open the door and lock the door. Because they didn't want the kids to be inside. Same way at Ursula and Carmen. We drive up. It's no use to come on ahead of time at Ursula and Carmen. You had to wait until the sister come and lock the door. Up there the sisters handle the scenery, turn on the lights and do everything. I played up there many times. They liked me. I was a gentleman. And they all sit in a row and they looked like a lot of penguins. And I'd play I Believe. You know I Believe? Oh, he's religious. I believe. And Al Black would get up and say it in his unsatan baritone. No, I love Al. I took Al. I was living in Lakeview and a handsome young man comes and knocks on the door and he's called and he says, man, can I get you interested? And a floral lamp. I guess you wonder what that tall lamp did. But you know why I got that thing? So I can read my paper. I have to have my paper with my coffee or I'm miserable. So this young man knocks me out and I come to the door. He didn't know that but the night before I had been out of the suburban going to scowlting the band. I wanted to scowl Ponds off of Ponds. I wasn't a scholar of Al Blanco. I had heard that Pons was good. I said, do you want a guitar? Get the Pons. So I got there and I talked to him back, I didn't let anybody know I was in a joint, and they did a jam session. Red Mackie had the band, I believe. You heard of Red Mackie.
